text:
Priya (CSM): Heads-up: Skywell needs final SLA wording for go-live on Friday. We must confirm uptime, latency SLOs, and an example credit calc before Legal signs. Can we align today?
Diego (Solutions): I can whip up the customer one-pager. Suggest calling out a 30-day onboarding window with relaxed latency SLOs and explicit degraded-mode behavior.
Nate (Eng): From runtime telemetry — initial cold-run p95 is ~280ms for this model under their trial traffic. With KV-cache priming and batching we can target 230ms by day 14. Recommend p95 280ms (0-14d), 230ms (15-90d).
Ava (Onboarding): I'll run the first-week health emails and schedule the SRE enablement call. Who owns the alert runbook?
Priya (CSM): Ava please own the runbook. Diego own the one-pager. Nate, can you provide the metrics dashboard link and the raw sample numbers for the examples?
Nate (Eng): Yep — pushing metrics feed to their team live. Dashboard: https://observability.redwood.com/d/skywell/overview. I'll attach a clip of 72h p95 numbers to the doc.
Diego (Solutions): Draft SLO snippet I'll include:

```
Metric | Target | Window
------|--------|-------
Uptime | 99.95% | 30d
Gen latency p95 | 280ms (0-14d) -> 230ms (15-90d) | 30d rolling
Error rate | <0.3% | 30d
```

Priya (CSM): Credit formula we typically use is proportional to missed uptime multiplied by invoice period, with min thresholds. Example worked numbers needed so customer understands impact.
Nate (Eng): Example: If observed uptime = 99.80% vs SLO 99.95% then uptime shortfall = 0.15% -> credit = shortfall * invoice_factor (our standard multiplier = 1.0) -> credit = 0.15% of monthly bill. I'll add an example table for common shortfall levels.
Maya (Legal): Quick check: if Diego's pager deviates from the standard SLA template, flag it. I need a one-line rationale for any deviations for the contract amendment.
Diego (Solutions): Will note deviations (onboarding window + staged latency targets) and rationale: initial cache warmup and progressive tuning.
Ava (Onboarding): I'll include an escalation flow: P0 -> on-call SRE, P1 -> Solutions lead (Diego), P2 -> CSM (Priya). Also include who triggers credits.
Priya (CSM): OpsBot please attach the canonical SLA template and the monthly report template we use.
OpsBot: Attached: /policies/sla_template_v3.pdf, /reports/slo_monthly_example.xlsx
Diego (Solutions): Timeline: I upload first draft this afternoon to Drive, Priya review tonight, Maya reviews legal tomorrow morning, Nate confirms metrics feed by Wed. Ava schedules enablement for Wed afternoon.
Priya (CSM): Sounds good. Also add a short 'what to expect during trial' section so Skywell knows we'll be tuning for 2 weeks and may request temporary increased capacity if needed. That helps manage renewal risk.
Nate (Eng): One more note: include fallback model mapping so if the primary model hits high latency we can route to a smaller faster variant — reduces p95 at cost of lower quality. I'll add the mapping.
Diego (Solutions): Uploaded draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/skywell-sla-draft-2026
Ava (Onboarding): Starting runbook now, will share first pass in #eng-ops later today.
Priya (CSM): Thanks all. I'll consolidate comments after Diego's upload and ping Legal once Maya gives the thumbs up. :thumbsup:
